feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 0 (score 63.0, best so far) used the same controller I have kept: kp 3.0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.5, last_direction recovery, and linear weights. All 60 trials ended off track, with about 1.0 line-loss event per run on the s-bend and slalom and max_error 0.062 to 0.066 m. Iteration 1 (kp 4.5, kd 0.3, 0.10 m track, 0.6 kg) scored 53.7, so higher gain and a narrower track did not help. Iteration 2 (span ±0.04 m, 0.5 kg, 0.12 m body) scored 46.5, the lowest, and changing several variables at once made it impossible to tell which one hurt. So the sensor offset is the next variable to test, and the controller is held fixed. If the next race shows line-loss events falling below about 0.5 per run and max_error staying under 0.06 m for longer, keep y = 0.07 m and try sensor_size 0.008 to sharpen the edge reading. If line losses stay at 1.0 per run with max_error still at or above 0.06 m, the forward offset is not the limit, and the next lever is mass (0.4 to 0.5 kg with body_length 0.12 m), since yaw inertia is the remaining untested variable with a single change. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with the forward offset, the extra lead is causing overshoot, so return y to 0.06 m rather than changing the mass.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events fall below 0.5 per run with max_error under 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom, keep sensor y = 0.07 m and try sensor_size 0.008 m to reduce blur at the sharpest bends (iteration 0 at 0.012 m had 1.0 line losses per run).

If line losses stay at 1.0 per run with max_error still at or above 0.06 m, try mass 0.5 kg with body_length 0.12 m, one change at a time, to cut yaw inertia; iteration 0 (0.7 kg) and iteration 2 (0.5 kg, span ±0.04 m) show that mass changes alone were not tested in isolation.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with the y = 0.07 m offset, return y to 0.06 m, since the added lead may be causing overshoot; iteration 0 showed steering_oscillation of 0.13 to 0.15 at y = 0.05 m.
